definition: a young horse, especially one less than a year old

collocations.example: The mare stood protectively beside her newborn foal in the field.
The farmer taught his daughter how to raise a foal properly.

definition: people or things treated as mere material to be used up for some purpose

collocations.example: The young recruits were sent to the front as cannon fodder.
The celebrity's divorce became easy fodder for gossip columnists.

definition: to take back property because the owner has not repaid the loan on it

collocations.example: The bank moved to foreclose on the property last month.
The lender threatened to foreclose after three missed payments.

definition: the finger next to the thumb; the index finger

collocations.example: She picked up the coin between her thumb and forefinger.
He pointed with a forefinger toward the far corner of the room.

definition: the ability to predict and prepare for what will happen in the future

collocations.example: She had the foresight to save money before losing her job.
Poor planning and a lack of foresight caused the project to fail.

definition: to prevent something from happening by taking action first

collocations.example: Good planning can forestall problems before they become serious.
The company acted quickly to forestall a strike by its workers.

definition: to leave someone or something completely, especially when you should stay

collocations.example: A loyal person would never forsake a friend in trouble.
He vowed never to forsake his family, no matter what happened.

definition: direct and honest in saying what you think

collocations.example: She answered every question in a forthright manner.
The manager was forthright about the company's financial difficulties.

definition: a wide road built for fast travel, with no traffic lights or crossings

collocations.example: Traffic on the freeway was heavy during the morning rush hour.
They sped along a busy freeway toward the airport.

definition: extremely cold

collocations.example: Frigid temperatures kept most people indoors throughout the week.
The swimmers shivered as they entered the frigid water of the lake.

definition: a woman's or girl's dress

collocations.example: She wore a light summer frock to the garden party.
The little girl twirled happily in her new frock.

definition: a soft, sweet candy made from sugar, butter, and milk

collocations.example: She made a tray of rich chocolate fudge for the party.
He offered me a piece of fudge from the box.

definition: done secretly and quietly to avoid being noticed

collocations.example: He cast a furtive glance over his shoulder before leaving.
Her furtive movements made the guard suspicious.

definition: the main body of an aircraft, where passengers and cargo are carried

The explosion left a gaping hole in the fuselage.

definition: relating to a galaxy or galaxies

The distances in space are measured on a galactic scale.

definition: a circle of flowers and leaves worn or hung as a decoration

collocations.example: The dancers wore a garland of flowers around their necks.
They hung a garland above the doorway to welcome guests.

definition: to gather or collect something, such as support or attention

Her research garnered attention from scientists around the world.

definition: a long, deep cut or wound

He was bleeding from a gash on his head after the accident.

definition: too brightly colored or decorated in a way that is not tasteful

She wore gaudy jewelry that clashed with her simple dress.

definition: very thin and bony, especially because of illness or worry

collocations.example: Illness had left him with a pale, gaunt face.

definition: friendly and cheerful

collocations.example: Our genial host made every guest feel welcome.
He greeted us with a genial smile and a warm handshake.

definition: a person who is not Jewish

The ancient city was home to both Jews and Gentiles.

definition: the science that studies the physical processes and structure of the Earth

collocations.example: Her degree focused on the study of geophysics and earthquakes.
He teaches at the university's geophysics department.

definition: a garden plant with red, pink, or white flowers

collocations.example: She placed a pot of geraniums on the windowsill.
Bright red geraniums bloomed along the front of the house.

definition: relating to old people and their medical care

collocations.example: The hospital opened a new ward for geriatric care.
She specializes in geriatric medicine at the city clinic.

definition: (of a seed) to begin to grow

collocations.example: These seeds germinate quickly in warm, moist soil.
The flowers we planted should germinate in spring.

definition: to carry developing young inside the body before birth

collocations.example: Elephants gestate for nearly two years before giving birth.
The twin calves gestated slowly inside their mother.

definition: feeling dizzy, as if everything is spinning

collocations.example: I began to feel giddy after spinning around so fast.
Looking down from the tower, she felt giddy from the height.

definition: a small round drop of liquid or a soft substance

collocations.example: A globule of oil floated on the surface of the water.
Tiny globules of fat formed on top of the soup.

definition: to look at someone in an angry way

collocations.example: He glowered at the referee after the unfair call.
She sat in the corner and glowered angrily at everyone.

definition: sad and quiet; in low spirits

collocations.example: He sat at the table with a glum face all evening.
Why do you look so glum this morning?

definition: a drinking cup with a stem and base, usually for wine

collocations.example: She filled each wine goblet before the guests arrived.
The knight raised a silver goblet to toast the king.

definition: something that people want very much and try hard to achieve

collocations.example: A cheap, clean fuel is the holy grail of energy research.
Scientists continue their search for the holy grail of cancer treatment.

definition: to form something into small grains or particles

collocations.example: The machine will granulate the sugar into fine crystals.
The powder is processed until it granulates into tiny grains.

definition: a large round yellow citrus fruit with a slightly bitter taste

collocations.example: She drinks a glass of grapefruit juice every morning.
He ate half a grapefruit with his breakfast.

definition: done without good reason and often causing harm or offense

collocations.example: The film was criticized for its gratuitous violence.

definition: green leaves, plants, and trees

The hall was decorated with flowers and greenery for the wedding.

definition: very serious and causing great pain or suffering

definition: a metal frame with bars placed over an opening for protection

definition: a small complaint about something

collocations.example: My only gripe about the job is the long hours.
Slow internet is a common gripe among the students.

definition: a medium-sized bird hunted for sport and food

collocations.example: The restaurant served roast grouse as its special dish.
They traveled north every autumn to shoot grouse.

definition: the thick, worm-like young form of an insect

definition: sounding rough and low

She gave a gruff reply in a low, raspy tone.

definition: a low, bubbling sound made by moving water or liquid

collocations.example: We heard a gurgle of water running through the pipes.
We relaxed to the gentle gurgle of a stream nearby.

definition: to argue in order to agree on a lower price

She haggled with the vendor until he lowered the cost.

definition: unlucky and often facing trouble

collocations.example: The scam targeted hapless victims who trusted the caller.
Our hapless hero stumbled from one disaster to the next.

definition: strict and refusing to change one's position

Critics attacked the party's hardline policy on immigration.

definition: the group of wives or women who lived in a Muslim household in the past

collocations.example: The sultan's many wives lived in the royal harem.
The ancient ruler was said to keep a large harem.

definition: to remind people of something from the past (used with 'back')

collocations.example: The design harks back to the styles of the 1950s.
It is a tradition that harks back many centuries.

definition: a heavy farming tool with metal teeth used to break up soil

collocations.example: The farmer pulled a disc harrow across the field.
They used a horse to drag a harrow over the soil.

definition: a dish of chopped cooked meat and potatoes fried together

collocations.example: She ordered eggs with a side of hash browns.
The diner is famous for its corned beef hash.

definition: to try to persuade someone to leave their job for another company

collocations.example: The firm works hard to headhunt top talent from rivals.
She was headhunted by a major bank last year.

definition: in a reckless and hurried way, without thinking carefully

collocations.example: He rushed headlong into marriage after knowing her a month.

definition: progress or forward movement, especially when it is difficult

collocations.example: The negotiators are finally making headway on the deal.
Police have made little headway in solving the crime.

definition: a shape like a spiral or a twisted coil

The staircase formed a graceful helix of stone steps.

definition: from this time on; from now on

Henceforth all visitors must sign in at the front desk.

definition: a chemical used to kill unwanted plants, especially weeds

collocations.example: Farmers spray herbicide to control weeds in their fields.
A selective herbicide kills weeds without harming the crop.

definition: in this document or statement (used in formal writing)

collocations.example: The terms contained herein apply to all customers.
Please follow the rules set forth herein.

definition: a belief or opinion that strongly disagrees with accepted beliefs

collocations.example: The scholar was accused of heresy by the church.
He was punished for spreading religious heresy.

definition: a small problem or delay that is usually temporary

collocations.example: The launch went smoothly apart from one minor hiccup.

definition: a title used when speaking to or about a royal person

collocations.example: "Thank you, Your Highness," the servant said with a bow.
The crowd cheered for His Royal Highness the prince.

definition: a chemical released by the body that causes allergic reactions

collocations.example: The body releases histamine in response to an allergy.
These tablets block histamine and reduce the itching.

definition: a garden tool with a thin blade used for breaking up soil and removing weeds

collocations.example: She loosened the soil with a garden hoe.
He used a hoe to clear the weeds between the rows.

definition: to shout loudly

collocations.example: The drowning man began to holler for help.
Don't holler at the children from across the yard.

definition: a holder for a gun, worn on a belt or under the arm

collocations.example: The officer kept his pistol in a leather gun holster.
He drew his weapon from the holster in one quick motion.

definition: (of a person) plain or not attractive in appearance

collocations.example: She had a plain, homely face but a warm smile.
The actor was rather homely, yet oddly charming on screen.

definition: a house and the land around it, especially a farm

collocations.example: They returned to the old family homestead for the holidays.
The settlers worked hard to build a homestead on the prairie.

definition: similarity in structure between things because they share a common origin

collocations.example: Scientists found a structural homology between the two proteins.
The study showed clear homology between the two species.

definition: a strong dislike of or prejudice against gay people

collocations.example: The campaign aims to combat homophobia in schools.
The group fights against homophobia and racism in sports.

definition: a noisy and violent person who causes trouble

definition: a word shouted to show joy, excitement, or approval

"Hooray for the champions!" the fans cheered loudly.

definition: a container that holds material and releases it from the bottom

collocations.example: Grain pours from the feed hopper into the machine.
Workers fill the hopper with raw plastic each morning.

definition: very unpleasant or nasty

collocations.example: A horrid smell came from the old refrigerator.
We stayed indoors because of the horrid weather.

definition: the large, abandoned body of a wrecked ship, vehicle, or building

collocations.example: The old ship was now just a rusting hulk on the shore.
Firefighters stared at the burnt-out hulk of the warehouse.

definition: a large, thick piece of something

collocations.example: She tore off a hunk of bread and dipped it in the soup.
He cut a thick hunk of cheese for the sandwich.

definition: unable to keep still or quiet; too active

collocations.example: The teacher struggled to calm the hyperactive child.
Some children become hyperactive after eating too much sugar.

definition: a sleep-like state in which a person responds easily to suggestions

collocations.example: Under hypnosis, she recalled details she had long forgotten.
He finally gave up smoking through hypnosis.

definition: having a calming effect that makes you feel sleepy or unable to look away

collocations.example: The soft music had an almost hypnotic effect on the crowd.
The drums beat with a slow, hypnotic rhythm.

definition: to put someone into a sleep-like state in which they respond to suggestions

collocations.example: The therapist tried to hypnotize the patient to ease her fears.
The stage performer will try to hypnotize a volunteer from the audience.

definition: the images and symbols used in art to represent a subject

collocations.example: The museum displayed paintings rich in religious iconography.
Scholars study the iconography of ancient temples.

definition: believing that things can be perfect, often more than is realistic

collocations.example: Idealistic young people joined the movement for change.

definition: seeming real but not actually existing or true

definition: very famous and admired for great achievements

collocations.example: She ended an illustrious career after forty years on stage.

definition: a person who leads prayers in a mosque

collocations.example: The local imam welcomed visitors to the mosque.
A respected imam spoke about peace at the gathering.

definition: to fill someone or something with a strong feeling or quality

collocations.example: The coach tried to imbue his players with confidence.

definition: to stop someone or something from moving

definition: a situation in which no progress is possible; a deadlock

definition: showing no emotion or feeling

definition: to force or strongly urge someone to do something

collocations.example: A sense of duty impelled him to speak out.

definition: impossible to get through or enter

collocations.example: The soldiers could not cross the impenetrable forest.

definition: to pretend to be another person in order to deceive people

collocations.example: He was arrested for trying to impersonate a police officer.

definition: to have a noticeable effect on something, often a limiting one

collocations.example: He never let his work impinge on his family life.

definition: to beg someone earnestly to do something

collocations.example: She implored him to stay just one more day.

definition: a lack of power or ability to change a situation; helplessness

definition: done without planning or preparation

collocations.example: She gave an impromptu speech when the main speaker fell ill.

definition: to make someone unable to work or function normally

definition: to make someone appear guilty of a crime

collocations.example: He refused to answer in case he might incriminate himself.

definition: a sudden attack on or entry into an area, especially by an enemy

collocations.example: The border village feared another military incursion.
